item.title: Six Generations: Mapping My Family Tree
item.description:
Last week, I found an old, crumpled piece of paper in my grandmother’s house. It was a hand-drawn family tree, barely legible, with names and dates scribbled in fading ink. That fragile document, torn and worn by time, contained six generations of my family’s history.

I decided to digitize it, not just to preserve the information, but to truly understand the web of connections that brought me here.

The Journey of a Name

My surname is Monteiro, but that’s only part of the story. Behind it lies a tapestry of names: Pereira, Costa, Lopes, Silva. Each one represents a branch, a marriage, a choice made by people I never met but who shaped who I am.
